pairs: Respondens autem Job, ait:
Then Job answered by saying:
Nunc quoque in amaritudine est sermo meus,
Now again my conversation is in bitterness,
et manus plagæ meæ aggravata est super gemitum meum.
and the force of my scourging weighs more heavily on me because of my mourning.
Quis mihi tribuat ut cognoscam et inveniam illum,
Who will grant me that I might know and find him,
et veniam usque ad solium ejus?
and that I may approach even to his throne?
Ponam coram eo judicium,
I would place judgment before his eye,
et os meum replebo increpationibus:
and my mouth would fill with criticism,
ut sciam verba quæ mihi respondeat,
so that I may know the words that he will answer me
et intelligam quid loquatur mihi.
and understand what he will say to me.
Nolo multa fortitudine contendat mecum,
I do not want him to contend with me with much strength,
nec magnitudinis suæ mole me premat.
nor to overwhelm me with the bulk of his greatness.
Proponat æquitatem contra me,
Let him show fairness in response to me,
et perveniat ad victoriam judicium meum.
and let my judgment reach to victory.
Si ad orientem iero,
If I go to the east,
non apparet;
he does not appear;
si ad occidentem,
if I go to the west,
non intelligam eum.
I will not understand him.
Si ad sinistram,
If I turn to the left,
quid agam?
what can I do?
non apprehendam eum;
I will not take hold of him.
si me vertam ad dexteram,
If I turn myself to the right,
non videbo illum.
I will not see him.
Ipse vero scit viam meam,
Truly,
et probavit me quasi aurum quod per ignem transit.
he knows my way and has tested me like gold that passes through fire.
Vestigia ejus secutus est pes meus:
My feet have been following his footsteps;
viam ejus custodivi,
I have kept to his way
et non declinavi ex ea.
and have not strayed from it.
A mandatis labiorum ejus non recessi,
I have not withdrawn from the commands of his lips,
et in sinu meo abscondi verba oris ejus.
and the words of his mouth I have hidden in my sinews.
Ipse enim solus est,
For he is alone,
et nemo avertere potest cogitationem ejus:
and no one is able to disturb his intention;
et anima ejus quodcumque voluit,
and whatever his spirit wills,
hoc fecit.
that he accomplishes.
Cum expleverit in me voluntatem suam,
And when he fulfills his will in me,
et alia multa similia præsto sunt ei.
many other similar ones will also be present with him.
Et idcirco a facie ejus turbatus sum,
And, for this reason, I have been troubled at his presence,
et considerans eum,
and, when I consider him,
timore sollicitor.
I am approached by fear.
Deus mollivit cor meum,
God has weakened my heart,
et Omnipotens conturbavit me.
and the Almighty has confused me.
Non enim perii propter imminentes tenebras,
Yet I have not perished because of the threatening darkness,
nec faciem meam operuit caligo.
nor has gloom covered my face.
